resource.name: aws_redshift_resource_policy
resource.description: Creates a new Amazon Redshift Resource Policy.
resource.llm_summary: The `aws_redshift_resource_policy` Terraform resource enables the creation and management of resource policies for Amazon Redshift, allowing users to define fine-grained access controls and permissions for Redshift clusters and data sharing. Common use cases include securing sensitive data, enforcing compliance requirements, and enabling cross-account access to Redshift resources. Users can configure policies to control actions like data sharing, cluster management, and integration with other AWS services, ensuring robust security and governance for Redshift environments.

examples.title: Basic Usage
examples.llm_summary: This example demonstrates how to configure an `aws_redshift_resource_policy` to grant permissions for Redshift inbound integration using a JSON-encoded IAM policy. It showcases the use of the `policy` and `resource_arn` arguments to define access control for a specific Redshift cluster namespace ARN.

arguments.name: id
arguments.llm_summary: The `id` argument in the `aws_redshift_resource_policy` resource allows users to specify a unique identifier for the resource policy, typically used to reference or manage the policy within Terraform configurations. While optional, setting this argument can help users track and organize policies, especially in environments with multiple Redshift resource policies.

arguments.name: policy
arguments.description: (Required) The content of the resource policy being updated.
arguments.llm_summary: The `policy` argument in the `aws_redshift_resource_policy` resource allows users to define the JSON-formatted resource policy that governs access control for Redshift resources. By setting this argument, users can specify permissions, roles, and conditions to manage security and compliance, ensuring controlled access to Redshift clusters and related resources.

arguments.name: resource_arn
arguments.description: (Required) The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the account to create or update a resource policy for.
arguments.llm_summary: The `resource_arn` argument specifies the Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the Redshift resource for which a resource policy is being created or updated. By defining this required identifier, users can associate access control policies with a specific Redshift resource, enabling fine-grained permissions management to meet security and compliance goals.
